one_line: Ancient Sanskrit prosody master who used binary-like methods to enumerate poetic meters.

appearance.age_look: Appears about 35–40, lean scholar’s build with upright, composed posture.
appearance.face: Oval face, medium brown complexion, sharp observant eyes, straight nose, neatly trimmed short beard and mustache; default expression is calm, mildly curious, as if silently analyzing patterns.
appearance.hair: Deep black, shoulder-length straight hair parted in the middle and smoothed back, tied into a low, neat knot at the nape; simple narrow white cloth headband encircling the forehead, no extra ornament.
appearance.costume: Early Indian Brahmin scholar attire: a plain off‑white cotton dhoti wrapped to the ankles and neatly pleated in front, a light saffron cotton uttariya shawl draped over both shoulders and across the chest, bare forearms with modest wooden bead bracelets, simple leather sandals, and a small cloth belt tying the dhoti at the waist; no embroidery, mostly solid colors in fine but unostentatious weave.
appearance.signature: A rectangular palm‑leaf manuscript bundle bound with a thin cord, held carefully in one hand, with a single smooth wooden counting stick in the other hand used to mark heavy and light syllables.

ref_desc: Pingala is a lean, medium-brown 35–40-year-old with shoulder-length black hair in a low knot, off-white dhoti, saffron shawl, simple sandals, palm-leaf manuscript bundle, and a wooden counting stick, colored in off-white, saffron, brown, and black tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of Pingala: a lean, medium-brown man appearing about 35–40 with an oval face, sharp thoughtful eyes, straight nose, and a neatly trimmed short beard and mustache. His deep black hair is shoulder-length, straight, parted in the middle, smoothed back, and tied into a low knot at the nape, with a narrow white cloth headband encircling his forehead. He wears an early Indian Brahmin scholar outfit: a plain off-white cotton dhoti wrapped down to the ankles with clean pleats, tied at the waist with a subtle cloth belt, and a light saffron cotton uttariya shawl draped over both shoulders and across his chest, leaving only his forearms bare. His feet are in simple leather sandals, and his arms have modest wooden bead bracelets. In one hand he holds a rectangular bundle of palm-leaf manuscripts bound with a thin cord; in the other he carries a smooth wooden counting stick used for marking heavy and light syllables. Keep the design modest and historically grounded, with dominant colors of off-white, saffron orange, medium brown skin and wood accents, and black hair, shown from multiple angles to emphasize his consistent face, hair knot, draped garments, and scholarly props.
